title: The Tent Has Been to Wales
genre: 70s UK soft-rock with sax hook (10cc and Gerry Rafferty lineage)
subject: a man who lent his two-man tent to a friend, who lent it to a cousin, and it has now slept nine strangers across three countries while he has never used it
caption: 70s UK soft-rock with a sax hook, glossy AM-radio studio production. Chorus-pedal clean electric guitar arpeggios, Fender Rhodes electric piano, melodic fretless bass, alto saxophone hook in the choruses, light congas and a tight snare. Warm analog compression, layered harmony vocals on the chorus. Male lead, smooth light baritone, wry deadpan delivery that stays clearly sung. Clear full voice, every word enunciated, steady sung melody on every line. 112 BPM, E major. Breezy, good-humoured mood. No rap, no autotune, no heavy distortion, no synth bass, no drum machine.
lyrics:
[Intro - chorus-pedal guitar, Rhodes, light congas]

[Verse 1]
I lent my tent to Dave in June
He said he'd have it back by noon
Dave gave it to his cousin Jo
Jo took it where the sheep all go

[Pre-Chorus]
A postcard came from Aberystwyth
Wish you were here, it said, and sorry

[Chorus]
The tent has been to Wales
It's been to Wales without me
Nine people slept inside it
And not one of them was me

[Verse 2]
A man named Piet in Rotterdam
Has patched it up with duct tape and jam
A girl in Cork I've never met
Sent me a photo of it wet

[Chorus]
The tent has been to Wales
It's been to Rotterdam and Cork
Nine people slept inside it
I just wanted one night in it

[Bridge - guitar alone, then congas]
I only asked to borrow it back
Dave says Friday, it's on the motorway

[Chorus]
The tent has been to Wales
And now it's coming home to me
Ten people will have slept inside it
And it's me, I'm the tenth, finally

[Outro - sax and guitar trade lines, fade]
The tent has been to Wales
Pitch it in the garden, I'll be fine
